title: timed mock interviews and spaced problem rehearsal
concepts: A mock interview simulates the full task cycle: clarify the contract, propose an approach, compare alternatives, implement, test, analyze complexity, and communicate tradeoffs.
Timed practice should allocate time for understanding and planning as well as coding; rushing directly to implementation often hides a wrong interpretation.
During implementation, narrate meaningful decisions and invariants while keeping the explanation concise enough to leave time for validation.
When stuck, make uncertainty explicit, reduce the problem, construct a tiny example, or return to a correct baseline before attempting an optimization.
A post-session review records what was misunderstood, which invariant or pattern was missed, which tests were absent, and one concrete correction for the next attempt.
Spaced re-solving schedules a problem again after a delay and requires reconstructing the method from memory rather than rereading a solution immediately.
Practice difficulty should increase gradually across patterns and constraints; repeating only familiar easy problems can create false confidence.
A progress log tracks solve time, hint dependence, correctness, explanation quality, and re-solve success, but the measurements guide practice rather than define ability.
